note: Several lines hold stacked slips (07:59-08:22: future + adjective gender + ykoon gender; 24:10-24:34: word + tense + preposition) - each is its own row. The name Kano does not appear in the text. No added rows; agreed rows A1-A27 all fit the transcript.

row.medi_said: So الواجب عندو تلات سو-- أسول-- أو-- Hold on. أسئلة.
row.amal_said: صح. فيو ثلاث أسئلة. ... فيو، in it. ... It doesn't have. There's in it.
row.why: He used عندو (possession) for questions inside the homework; Amal recast فيو and explained 'It doesn't have. There's in it'; he took it ('instead of عندي، فيو'). The fix is the small word عند vs في (preposition + pronoun), so grammar D1, not a new lexical item.

rulings.why: Both readers saw it; the fix is preposition choice (عند -> في), so grammar D1.

rulings.why: Real: Mm-mm + minni, and he confirmed he said ma3i.

row.medi_said: bifikru el lugha muhim ilhom. ... Language is gonna be important, yeah.
row.amal_said: So it's going to be. So
row.right: beyfakkru el-lu8a ra7 tkoon muhemma ilhom
row.why: He meant 'language is going to be important' (said so in English) but left out ra7 + ykoon; Amal's English 'So it's going to be' prompted, he said 'rah fikun' and she confirmed 'راح'.
row.english: They think the language is going to be important for them.

rulings.why: Two slips sit in this line: the missing future (prompted by 'So it's going to be') and the feminine adjective (prompted later by 'لغة as well', ruled in D6). r1's B13 reading is the one this prompt targets; r2's A8 reading is D6.

row.medi_said: Uh, rah fikun. ... Going to be rah.
row.why: لغة is feminine so the adjective is muhemma; Amal's 'بس لغة as well' prompted, he said 'Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema'.
row.english: It is going to be important.

rulings.why: The fix he actually made after her hint is muhim -> muhema (A8). The ykoon piece is ruled separately in D7.

row.medi_said: Oh, it's feminine. Rah fikun muhema ilhom.
row.why: Her hint 'لغة as well' came right after his 'rah fikun' (masc ykoon); he fixed only the adjective and kept fikun; with feminine لغة it is tkoon (her chat). Medium: the engine may blur ykun/tkun.
row.english: It is going to be important.

rulings.why: Her feminine hint followed 'rah fikun' directly, so it covers the verb too; he fixed the adjective but not ykoon -> tkoon.

row.medi_said: il modara. No, modara is present... moraja. ... Mak. Does it have a K in it? ... maba nasito.
row.amal_said: Do you remember the word for future؟ ... مـ-مس... مستقبل.
row.why: Amal asked for the word for future; he guessed and himself rejected modara (present) and moraja, said he forgot, and she gave مستقبل (sheet: future | Musta2bal). He never used a wrong word in his own sentence first, so it is a didn't-know (tier 0). The 09:35 'fi il modara' is a repeat of the same moment.

rulings.why: Tier 0: answering her 'do you remember the word for future?' with guesses he rejected himself is a didn't-know, not a wrong word used in a sentence.

Not an error: 'Shwe min kbar libisna costume bas kul il zgar' reads fine without ma ('some of the adults dressed up, but all the kids did'), and he said it the same way again at 11:11. Only her chat has ma lebsu, and chat alone is not a correction (GR-19). The person slip (libisna -> libsu) is agreed row A5.
Cannot be verified: the engine's 'أسر مارا الجاي' most likely hides 'el-marra el-jaay' (a slurred el-). Amal answered حلو، ممتاز and only her chat spells it; no voiced signal.

row.medi_said: Okay. أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب، أنا بأسب لهم
row.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Mm-mm. And about it was I get angry.
row.why: For 'upset for them' he used ba3asseb (engine بأسب; sheet: i get angry | Ana ba3asseb); Amal said Mm-mm twice and that his word means 'I get angry'; he moved to داية it = tdaaya2et (sheet: i feel upset about / for someone | Ana batDaaya2 3ala).

rulings.why: Three separate fixes sit here: the word (angry vs upset, this row), the tense (D12) and the preposition (D13). Her 'And about it was I get angry' targets the word, so vocab-A tier 1.

row.why: The sentence is past ('I got upset') but he used a present b- verb; Amal stressed 'I got', he said 'Oh, you're right' and used the past daya2et.

rulings.why: r1's tense row; r2's preposition piece is ruled in D13.

row.medi_said: أنا بأسب منهم. ... أنا بأسب لهم
row.amal_said: Mm-mm. I got upset for them. ... Mm-mm. ... Saħħ.
row.why: Feeling upset for someone takes 3ala (sheet: Ana batDaaya2 3ala); he tried min, then li, Amal said Mm-mm to both; he reasoned to ala and she said Saħħ. Medium: her Mm-mm also covers the wrong verb.

rulings.why: Real: min and li both drew Mm-mm before he got ala confirmed (25:16).

row.amal_said: No, you don't need anything. If you do-- If you would want to put something, it would be in, in anything.
row.why: He started to put ala before 'the end of the movie'; Amal said no preposition is needed (or fi). He was cut off mid-phrase, so low.
row.english: ...for them at the end of the movie.

rulings.why: Voiced 'No, you don't need anything' after a word he did say; low because the phrase was unfinished.

row.medi_said: منيح بس ما حبيت الـ آخرو.
row.amal_said: No ال. Why? ... Why no ال؟
row.chat: awal el-felem mnee7 bas maa 7abbait aa5ro
row.why: A word with a pronoun ending is already definite, so no el- in front (aa5ro); Amal said 'No ال. Why?', he answered 'cause it's conjugated'.
row.english: ...but I didn't like the end of it.

rulings.why: Same slip for both readers. The rule applied is el- never sits on a word with a possessive ending (A4); A20 (aa5er + possessive = end of) as bucket2.

row.medi_said: Would it be مواسف here or would it be ياسر؟
row.amal_said: بيعصب بس كان أو كانوا cuz أخبار is multiple news.

rulings.why: He asked which word; she supplied بيعصب -> didn't-know, tier 0. The كان -> كانوا part of her line is agreed row A21.

row.amal_said: الحفلة؟ [تضحك] I wish I would be a حفلة.
row.why: He said الحفلة (the party) for the war; Amal echoed it laughing ('I wish it would be a حفلة'), so he did say it, and he fixed it to 'Oh my God. الحرب' (sheet: war | 7arb).
row.english: The war is going to get worse.

rulings.why: Her laughing echo proves he said حفلة; a different word, fixed only after her echo.

row.chat: el-ishi el-mufaddal 3indi lamma ana at6alla3 3ala el-6abi3a
row.why: 'Look at' is at6alla3 3ala (sheet: i look at | Ana bat6alla3 3ala); Amal echoed his verb and added 'at', so she was prompting the missing على; he said 'أتطلع على الطبيعة' and 'I forgot to say it'. The engine likely wrote أطلع for أتطلع; her echo accepts the verb and targets the preposition.

rulings.why: Her prompt is the English preposition 'at', so it is the fixed-preposition rule (D2), not a wrong word.
A question, not a slip: 'إنه or اللي...' was him asking which linking word to use; Amal answered that none is needed. A question about the rule is neither a slip nor a use (reader brief).

row.amal_said: close. ... التاني. ... Because صحابك is definitive.
row.why: After a definite noun (pronoun ending) taani takes el- (A14: el-noun el-taani); Amal said 'close', gave التاني and explained 'صحابك is definitive'. Her chat keeps the plural el-taanyeen.

rulings.why: A14 is the bucket written for exactly this (noun + el-taani).
Not an error: after 'I said kind', Amal herself said 'You could say last one' (18:21), so his آخر واحد is also valid.
Not an error: Amal's echo is the proof of what he said, and she repeated قرأت three times ('No, no. قرأت') - he said قرأت, not قريت. At most a hamza-pronunciation point (S4).

Not provable: her 'في ... in the morning' targets bi vs fi before الصباح (بالصباح is fine colloquially), not أوّل مرة. His later أوّل الصباح came after an unrelated stretch, not as a fix of her prompt.
Duplicate of D18 (same moment 48:49, same fix أطلع الطبيعة -> أتطلع على الطبيعة, same bucket D2).

row.why: To say 'my first day' with أول as an adjective the noun must carry the owner ending (يومي الأول); Amal's 'يوم هو' (engine; her pointing at the ending) prompted and he said يومي الأول, she said صح.
